children: The upcoming IPO of Mahanadi Coalfields, and the future listing of another subsidiary South Eastern Coal Fields will provide Coal India Ltd. with its capex requirements for the future, DIPAM Secretary Arunish Chawla told CNBC-TV18 exclusively in an interaction on Monday, November 16.

While Mahanadi Coalfields disclosed the price band of its ₹8,981 crore IPO earlier in the day, Chawla added that the next six months will see another Coal India subsidiary going public in the form of South Eastern Coalfields.

Chawla said the listing of Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd. (MCL), Coal India's largest and most profitable subsidiary, will provide the state-run miner with an initial capital inflow while opening up avenues for the subsidiary to access capital markets for its own expansion plans.
The DIPAM Secretary said Mahanadi Coalfields is also looking to enter coal gasification, which could help meet the requirements of other sectors, including fertilisers.
The company is exploring investments in downstream power generation in conjunction with the government of Odisha, he said.

The initial 10% offer-for-sale will provide proceeds to Coal India. However, Chawla said a further 15% stake could be available for Mahanadi Coalfields to raise capital for its own requirements, in line with applicable regulatory provisions, as Coal India brings its stake in the company down to 75%, the DIPAM Secretary added.

"We hope that this will give enough funds to Coal India to fund its direct operational needs on the renewable and green side, and that will help move Coal India from a pure holding to some to an entity which is both holding and has direct operations," Chawla said.

India is targeting ₹80,000 crore in disinvestment proceeds during the current financial year, of which ₹62,000 crore has already been raised. Chawla said they will meet the annual disinvestment target and are also hopeful of exceeding it..
Mahanadi Coalfields, which accounts for nearly 30% of Coal India's production and around 20% of India's total coal output, is being listed to improve its access to capital, Chawla said.
The company has significant capital requirements ahead, including investments in mining technology, mechanised mining, mechanised rail loading, clean coal technology and downstream power production.
The additional capital could support the company's expansion into clean coal technology, coal washeries, mechanised mining, rail loading infrastructure and downstream power production.
SECL IPO expected in the next six months
Coal India is also looking to monetise its stake in South Eastern Coalfields through a public listing, with Chawla expecting the IPO to come to market in the next six months.
The listing is expected to provide Coal India with another avenue to raise funds for its capital expenditure requirements, alongside the proceeds from the Mahanadi Coalfields IPO.
Coal India is expanding beyond its traditional coal mining operations, with plans to enter renewable energy and other businesses that require significant capital investments.
Chawla said the company's capital requirements are increasing as it looks to diversify into renewable energy, clean coal technology and other sectors.

title: DIPAM Secretary Arunish Chawla explains how Coal India will get its funding needs for the future: Exclusive
